☀️ Solar Sage AI

A drone-based Edge-AI system for condition-based solar panel cleaning — replacing blind, water-heavy maintenance with intelligent, targeted action.

🤖 Edge AI 🛩️ Drone-Based 👁️ OpenCV ⚡ ESP32 📊 Dashboard <1s Decision Latency 70%+ Water Savings 5 AI Agents 99% Uptime Target ## 🔍 The Problem

Solar operators at utility scale face a critical mismatch — panels are cleaned on fixed schedules, blind to actual dirt levels. This leads to:

  • 💧 Massive water waste — a 1 GW farm uses 12.5M+ litres/month on washing alone
  • 📅 Schedule blindness — clean panels get washed; genuinely dirty ones wait weeks
  • ⚠️ Physical degradation — frequent contact cleaning causes micro-cracks and shortens panel life
  • 📉 Fragmented decisions — without per-panel data, the dirtiest panels aren't prioritized
## 💡 Our Solution

Solar Sage AI is an autonomous "Inspect-to-Clean" system that uses drone imagery and edge AI to clean only what needs cleaning, when it needs cleaning.

📷 Perception Pipeline

RGB & thermal drone payload with OpenCV-based detection to capture and segment panel imagery in real time.

🧠 Edge Decision Layer

ESP32-driven control system classifying dirt levels and issuing cleaning commands with sub-second latency.

🤖 Multi-Agent Backend

Confidence, priority, benchmarking, ROI, and water-optimization agents that jointly decide when and where to clean.

🎯 Targeted Actuation

Servo-controlled, precision water application — replacing blanket cleaning cycles with surgical interventions.

📊 Live Dashboard

Per-panel dirt scores, efficiency gains, cost savings, and ROI reporting — all in a single monitoring interface.

🔄 CI/CD Pipeline

Automated builds and tests for the OpenCV pipeline and ESP32 firmware on every change, enabling safe iteration.

## ⚙️ Processing Pipeline 1 🛩️ Drone Capture

RGB & thermal imagery across the panel field

2 👁️ OpenCV Detection

Segment panels, detect surface dirt & debris

3 🧠 AI Decision

Score dirt 0–100, rank by cleaning priority

4 ⚡ ESP32 Execution

Servo & pump signals for targeted cleaning

5 ✅ Validate

Confirm cleaning, log metrics for ROI

docs.title: 🏗️ Architecture
docs.text: Solar Sage AI follows a five-stage pipeline architecture, from drone image capture through edge-AI classification to targeted actuation. The system decouples perception from decision-making, enabling scalable multi-drone coordination and low-latency cleaning triggers.

docs.title: System Overview
docs.text: The architecture is composed of three primary layers:

docs.title: 1. Perception Layer
docs.text:
• Drone Payload — RGB and thermal cameras capture high-resolution imagery of solar panel arrays
  • OpenCV Pipeline — Real-time image segmentation isolates individual panels and identifies dirt/debris regions
  • Feature Extraction — Colour and texture thresholds are computed for each panel surface

docs.title: 2. Decision Layer
docs.text:
• Dirt Scoring Engine — Each panel receives a score (0–100) based on heuristic feature analysis
  • Multi-Agent System — Five specialized agents collaborate:
    • Confidence Agent — Suppresses low-confidence detections
    • Priority Agent — Ranks panels by cleaning urgency
    • Benchmarking Agent — Compares against historical baselines
    • ROI Agent — Estimates return on cleaning investment
    • Water Optimization Agent — Minimizes resource usage

docs.title: 3. Actuation Layer
docs.text:
• ESP32 Controller — Receives cleaning commands and drives hardware
  • Servo Motors — Precision-target the water nozzle to specific panel regions
  • Pump Control — Delivers measured water volume based on dirt severity

docs.title: Technology Stack
docs.text:
👁️ Computer Vision

OpenCV for panel segmentation, dirt detection, and feature extraction from drone imagery.

⚡ Edge Computing

ESP32 microcontroller for sub-second decision-to-actuation latency with zero cloud dependency.

🐍 Python Ecosystem

NumPy, Pandas, and scikit-learn for scoring logic, agent coordination, and data analysis.

📊 Web Dashboard

Real-time monitoring interface for per-panel metrics, efficiency tracking, and ROI reporting.

🔄 CI/CD

GitHub Actions for automated builds, tests, linting, and deployment of firmware and backend.

🛩️ Drone Hardware

Standard flight platform with RGB/thermal payload for field-level panel inspection.

docs.title: Design Constraints
docs.text: Constraint Rationale Sub-1s decision latency Fully on-edge pipeline; no cloud round-trips Heuristic-first classification Explainable thresholds over black-box deep learning Standard flight hardware Deployability with commercially available drones Containerized deployment Reproducible dashboard and backend environments

docs.title: Project Phases
docs.text:
Phase 1 — Foundation Core Perception & Actuation Prototype

Drone image capture, OpenCV-based panel segmentation, basic dirt detection, and ESP32 servo/pump control prototype. CI pipeline setup with linting and basic tests.

Phase 2 — Integration End-to-End Detect-and-Clean Loop

Full pipeline integration: image → detection → scoring → actuation. Dirt scoring on a 0–100 scale with heuristic thresholds. Basic logging for latency measurement.

Phase 3 — Intelligence Multi-Agent Decision Layer

Deploy five specialized agents (confidence, priority, benchmarking, ROI, water optimization) that collaboratively determine cleaning actions.

Phase 4 — Dashboard Monitoring & ROI Reporting

Web-based dashboard showing per-panel dirt scores, efficiency gains, cost savings, and historical trends. Containerized deployment with CI/CD.

Phase 5 — Validation Field Testing & Benchmarking

Water, electrical, and dust tests on a test array. Before/after comparison against manual cleaning baseline. Publish evaluation metrics.

Stretch Goal Learned Classification

Replace heuristic thresholds with a trained model for improved edge-case accuracy. Multi-drone coordination for larger panel fields.

docs.title: Risks & Mitigations
docs.text: Risk Mitigation Low-light / glare reducing detection accuracy Combine RGB with thermal imaging; schedule flights in optimal lighting False-positive cleaning triggers Confidence agent suppresses low-confidence detections before actuation Hardware / weather delays Buffer window in final project phase for field-testing Measurement ambiguity Baseline measurements taken under matched conditions before comparison
